Whether through deception or desperation, Indians continue to be drawn into Russia's war in Ukraine. What can New Delhi do to protect its citizens from ending up fighting in Ukraine?
Gurpreet Singh Randhawa, a 40-year-old from Jalandhar in India's northern Punjab state, said he traveled to Russia for work after responding to a Facebook advertisement for a driving job at a garment factory.
But instead of finding work as a driver, he was sent to fight in Ukraine for the Russian armed forces .
After escaping from his unit, he surrendered to Ukrainian forces in November. He is now being held as a prisoner of war.
In an interview with Ukrainian YouTuber Volodymyr Zolkin, Randhawa described how, after arriving in Russia, he was taken to a military facility, made to sign a contract and sent for training. He said they confiscated his passport and phone. His account has not been independently verified.
He is the second Indian national known to have escaped the Russian military. Sahil Majothi, a 23-year-old from Gujarat, surrendered to Ukrainian forces in October 2025. He had joined the Russian military while serving a prison sentence in Russia, reportedly believing that military service would help him secure his release.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
The cases underline how little has changed since Prime Minister Narendra Modi raised the issue with Russian President Vladimir Putin during his visit to Moscow in July 2024 .
At the time, Putin assured him that Indians who were misled into joining the Russian army would be discharged. But the recruitment of Indians has continued.
In an October filing before the Supreme Court, India's Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said approximately 267 Indians have joined the Russian armed forces since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine .
Of these, 139 were discharged and 51 were killed. The whereabouts of the 77 others were unknown. Russian authorities have confirmed that seven of them are missing.
The problem extends beyond Indians who travel to Russia seeking civilian employment, only to find themselves exposed to recruitment networks and the dangers of a war zone.
The MEA has also highlighted cases of Indians knowingly enlisting in the Russian military for the supposed financial benefits on offer, believing they could later secure release through government intervention.
Some had also approached Indian authorities to renounce their citizenship and obtain Russian passports. "This is a dangerous path and is strongly discouraged by the government," the ministry said.
Former diplomat Anil Trigunayat said the growing movement of Indian workers to Russia presents both economic opportunities and new challenges for their protection.
"Inadequate oversight of recruitment networks could leave vulnerable workers exposed to exploitation," Trigunayat told DW.
He said Indian workers were often burdened by substantial recruitment fees and continued deductions from their salaries by intermediaries.
"Some of them had paid between 300,000 to 500,000 Indian rupees [$5,400 /€4,900] to Indian recruitment agents, and even while working in Russia, more than 30% of their agreed monthly salary was taken away by local and foreign agents," Trigunayat said.
The former diplomat added that some Indians who had overstayed their visas in Russia were particularly vulnerable. Military service was allegedly offered to earn substantial wages and regularize their immigration status.
Mohammad Sufiyan, from Hyderabad in the southern state of Telangana, said he was lured to Russia under false pretences and forced into active combat in Ukraine.
He had traveled abroad in search of employment and a better livelihood, but ended up in a war zone. He has since returned home to India .
"Many people are duped. Some decide it is better to seek citizenship than come back to India. It's a tough life, and people will go to any lengths to get some sort of employment," Sufiyan told DW.
Sufiyan's experience points to the economic desperation that makes such offers attractive, even when they carry the risk of being caught up in a war.
Rajan Kumar, a professor at the Center for Russian and Central Asian Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University's School of International Studies, said some Indians who traveled to Russia for work could find themselves caught up in the fighting without having joined the military.
"Some of them, they don't join the army, but they end up in the army region. They're caught in the crossfire," Kumar told DW.
He said India was negotiating with Moscow to secure the return of its citizens caught up in such situations. "Russia is very cooperative so far," he said.
India has been pressing Russia to take action, but the issue persists.
The recruitment efforts reflect Russia's need for more manpower for its nearly five-year war in Ukraine , and the limited influence New Delhi can exert over Moscow, despite the close political relationship between the two countries.
Mohsin Raza Khan, a professor at the Jindal School of International Affairs, told DW that Putin 's need to sustain the war effort was taking precedence over the concerns of a strategic partner.
He points out that the Russian president was reluctant to impose another mobilization on his own population for fear of domestic unrest.
"In these circumstances, sustaining the war effort appears to take precedence over concerns raised by India. Neither Modi nor New Delhi has sufficient leverage to change that," said Khan.
Khan also said the willingness of some Indians to enlist, and even consider giving up their citizenship, is down to the lack of decent employment opportunities at home.
"For young, educated men without contacts or connections, the chances of respectable employment are so low that the risks of a high casualty war are preferable," he said.

AJ Odudu said being called aggressive was "very harsh" and it was "an insane word" to use about her
More than 800 people have complained to the media regulator about an episode of ITV reality show I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here! in which Mariella Frostrup accused her campmate AJ Odudu of being "aggressive".
Ofcom said 887 people had filed complaints about Sunday's episode in relation to "alleged bullying behaviour" by Frostrup towards Odudu.
An Ofcom spokesperson told BBC News: "We are assessing the complaints against our rules, but are yet to decide whether or not to investigate."
The pair were seen clearing the air on Tuesday, with broadcaster Frostrup saying she was "sorry for calling you aggressive" and Odudu telling her it is "a strong word to use in casual scenarios, particularly towards black women".
Wayne Rooney tried to repair relations between AJ Odudu (left) and Mariella Frostrup on Sunday
Relations between the pair became fractious when Odudu attempted to help Frostrup cook on Saturday's episode.
Tensions flared further as they and other campmates discussed their friction and the cooking arrangements the following morning.
After fellow celebrities Wayne Rooney and Claire Sweeney tried to smooth the strained relationship in Sunday's episode, Frostrup told Odudu she was "making a drama out of a crisis" and that she had been "thrilled there was another person" who said they could cook.
Odudu responded: "You have a funny way of showing it, that's all," before Frostrup replied: "You see, that's just aggressive and that's what keeps happening."
Odudu said she felt being called aggressive was "very harsh".
Both women later had tearful conversations with other campmates, with Odudu saying "aggressive" was "an insane word" to use about her, while Frostrup said the pressure in the camp was "too much".
They included former BBC Radio 1 DJ Clara Amfo, who said: "Calling a black woman 'aggressive' when she is being anything else but is a classic microaggression."
Singer Beverley Knight wrote: "The word 'aggressive' feeds directly into the 'angry Black woman' trope. It IS hurtful and offensive."
Speaking on spin-off show I'm A Celebrity... Unpacked on Sunday, former campmate Jordan Banjo said Frostrup had handled the situation "poorly", but urged people to "give a bit of grace to Mariella, and everyone in the camp" because "you can't judge an abnormal situation by normal standards".
It is "a really weird situation that every single person's in, and I'm not sure if people go at stuff with the clearest head", he said, explaining: "You get these weird breakdowns, and I think that's what we're seeing."
Mariella Frostrup risked further tension when she told Odudu that "you don't take an apology well"
Frostrup apologised during an amicable conversation in Tuesday's episode.
Odudu told her being called "aggressive" was "triggering because in this world, navigating it as a person who looks like me can be difficult sometimes because my experience is that my emotions and my intent are completely misconstrued".
She added: "In same way that you are allowed to express yourself, I can't express myself in the same way. We're not granted the same freedom.
"You're allowed to be emotional and passionate, and I automatically go to 'aggressive'. There's no in-between. It's like I'm 'dramatic' and 'aggressive' and that's it.
"Whereas I feel like someone like you gets to go through all the emotions of life and all of those emotions are accepted and embraced and valid."
Frostrup replied that she thought being labelled "aggressive" was "a woman thing more than anything else".
"I think women who speak their mind and are forthright, that's 'aggressive', whereas a man who speaks his mind and is forthright is a 'strong man'," she said, but added that "I totally get that there's more" when race is involved.
Odudu responded: "I do definitely see your point and agree with it, but those words stick as well. Those words can stick for us. The moment passes for you and it doesn't pass for me."
Odudu replied: "Well, I wasn't being aggressive, so it shouldn't have been there."
Signs of friction resurfaced when Frostrup told Odudu that "you don't take an apology well".
Odudu replied that "of course" she had accepted her apology, before Frostrup accepted that "it's really important to me to understand why it's triggering".
Odudu added: "It's good you asked, but it's a strong word to use in casual scenarios, particularly towards black women."
An ITV statement said: "The production monitors everyone in camp 24/7 and if at any time we feel someone has overstepped the line by using inappropriate language or displaying unacceptable behaviour, we would take steps to intervene and speak to everyone involved.
"The duty of care for our contestants is of the utmost importance to us. We take the welfare of the celebrities very seriously and have measures in place to ensure they are supported at every stage of the process: before, during and after filming."

FILE - Senegal's Sadio Mane holds the trophy aloft as he celebrates with teammates after winning the Africa Cup of Nations final soccer match between Senegal and Morocco in Rabat, Morocco, Sunday, Jan. 18, 2026. Youssef Loulidi/AP hide caption
More than 10 months on from a chaotic, controversial final, Senegal is Africa's soccer champion once again.
Senegal won back the Africa Cup of Nations title in a legal fight on Tuesday after the Court of Arbitration for Sport overturned an earlier ruling which handed the trophy to Morocco.
Senegal won the Africa Cup on the field in Morocco in January and then lost it in a legal case in March because its players walked off the field in protest in second-half stoppage time.
CAS has now rejected that earlier ruling, based on referee Jean-Jacques Ndala's decision to let the game resume after the protest.
"The Court of Arbitration for Sport has delivered justice to sport," Senegalese soccer federation president Abdoulaye Fall said in a statement.
The legal battle may not be over yet after Morocco announced plans to appeal, likely to Switzerland's supreme court, in a challenge to the integrity of a senior CAS judge.
Tournament regulations said a team which refuses to play should be considered to have lost the game, but CAS said those rules were meant only for cases "when a team's conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently."
Ndala "did not err in law" when he resumed the game and had "sole authority" to make that call, CAS said, adding its three judges were unanimous.
"The panel acknowledged that the referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension," CAS said. "However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as 'arbitrary.' On the contrary, the referee's judgment did not appear to have been affected by factors external to the game."
Morocco's soccer federation detailed plans for an appeal that targets one of the three judges on the CAS panel.
In a statement, the Moroccan federation protested what it described as the court's failure to address potential integrity concerns, alleging "confirmed communication" between German arbitrator Ulrich Haas and Fall, the Senegalese soccer president, 48 hours before the decision was issued.
The CAS director general, Matthieu Reeb, acknowledged to reporters at the court in Lausanne that a Moroccan protest was received just minutes before the verdict was announced.
Reeb said the court's panel "in charge of petitions for challenge has conceded that there was not enough elements at this stage to postpone the notification of the award."
CAS verdicts can be challenged at Switzerland's supreme court, also in Lausanne, though only on limited procedural grounds of which a judge's integrity could be one.
Haas has been among the most respected and in-demand CAS judges in the past 20 years, selected by parties in storied cases involving Manchester City's beating a Champions League ban by UEFA, tennis star Simona Halep's doping case and Africa's Champions League final in 2019.
Patrick Kabou, a lawyer for the Senegalese Soccer Federation, called the alleged communication between Fall and Haas "unreal."
Senegal won the final 1-0 after extra time with chaos on the field and violent clashes in the stands. Even the ball boys were involved in scuffles as they tried to snatch towels that Senegal goalkeeper Edouard Mendy was using to keep his gloves dry.
The result was overturned two months later as a 3-0 default win for Morocco by an appeals panel appointed by the Confederation of African Football (CAF).
Senegal beat AFCON host nation Morocco after a 15-minute delay in play. At 0-0, Senegal's team walked off the field to protest Morocco being awarded a penalty kick in the last minute of regulation time.
Match referee Ndala of Congo eventually allowed the game to restart, Morocco's penalty by Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz — a slow chip shot known as a "Panenka" — was saved, and Senegal won in extra time.
The drama continued through the months of legal tussles. Senegal's players paraded with the trophy ahead of a game in March against Peru, even though Morocco was recognized as the champion at that point.
Both teams played at the World Cup believing themselves to be the rightful champion of Africa.
Senegal had the laws of the game on its side, and Morocco had the tournament regulations.
The laws of soccer state that referee decisions are final. CAS backed that position with its own "field of play" doctrine, that on-field calls by a referee generally can't be taken to the sports court.
"By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met — both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume," CAS said.
In the first legal case in March, CAF appeal judges cited AFCON tournament regulations that if a team "refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorization of the referee, it shall be considered loser and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition."
The CAS judges heard evidence at a one-day hearing last month and the court promised a verdict by the end of November with a full written ruling of its judges setting out reasons for their decision.
The next men's AFCON starts in June co-hosted by Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania. Morocco will aim to end a wait for the title which now stands at 50 years.
"Senegal won on the pitch, and the court simply confirmed what we all already knew: We are the real champions of Africa," said Mariama Sidibé, 35, an accountant in the capital, Dakar.
Sidibé said the dispute between Morocco and Senegal should now be left in the past.
"With all of this behind us, we should focus on what unites us now, and who knows, maybe Morocco can have its revenge on the field during the next AFCON this summer," she said.
"At the end of the day Morocco and Senegal are brothers," Sidibé added, referring to the countries' long shared close ties built on religion, trade and culture.
Sidi Sylla, a philosophy student at Dakar's main university, said the court's ruling was "not just a win for Senegal but for football in general."
CAS rulings have stripped many athletes of Olympic medals for doping, but it's rare to overturn the result of a major soccer competition.
CAS refused to change the results of the 2019 Asian Cup, dismissing an appeal that the star striker on winning team Qatar shouldn't have been eligible for the tournament.
A lengthy legal battle over the same year's African Champions League final also ended with the original winner, Esperance of Tunisia, taking the title after its opponent Wydad from Morocco refused to play on.
One notable CAS ruling on a team sport title came at the Winter Olympics in 2022. A doping case involving then-15-year-old Russian figure skater Kamila Valieva ended up with her disqualification, and the Russian team being dropped from gold to bronze in the team event.

Ofcom receives 887 complaints, while media figures accuse Frostrup of using ‘microaggression’ against Odudu
Almost 900 people have complained to the UK’s media regulator about an episode of ITV’s I’m A Celebrity … Get Me Out of Here! after the broadcaster Mariella Frostrup called her fellow campmate and presenter AJ Odudu “aggressive”.
Ofcom said 887 people had filed complaints in relation to “alleged bullying behaviour” by Frostrup, who has been accused by other black media figures of using a “microaggression” against Odudu.
The complaints relate to an exchange broadcast on Sunday which stemmed from an attempt by Odudu, who presents Big Brother, to help Frostrup cook dinner, shown on Saturday’s episode.
The issue of cooking came up again on Sunday, as campmates Wayne Rooney and Claire Sweeney attempted to improve relations between the two.
Frostrup, 64, accused Odudu, 38, of “making a drama out of a crisis” over the cooking arrangements, saying she was delighted to have some help. Odudu replied: “You have a funny way of showing it, that’s all.”
Frostrup responded: “You see, that’s just aggressive and that’s what keeps happening.”
Odudu said being called aggressive was “very harsh”. She later told campmates that describing her as “aggressive” was an “insane word” to use. Frostrup later said the pressure of being in the camp was “too much”.
An Ofcom spokesperson said: “We are assessing the complaints against our rules, but are yet to decide whether or not to investigate.”
ITV producers are reported to have intervened and spoken to Frostrup in the camp’s bush telegraph cabin. Frostrup later apologised to Odudu on Tuesday’s episode.
A host of TV personalities spoke out in defence of Odudu, including the Strictly Come Dancing judge Motsi Mabuse, the comedian Judi Love, and Will Best, who co-hosts Big Brother with Odudu.
Clara Amfo, the former BBC Radio 1 DJ, said: “Calling a black woman ‘aggressive’ when she is being anything else but is a classic microaggression.”
The singer Beverley Knight wrote online: “The word ‘aggressive’ feeds directly into the ‘angry Black woman’ trope. It IS hurtful and offensive.”
Others have urged viewers to consider the pressures of being on reality TV. The dancer Jordan Banjo, a former campmate, said while Frostrup had not handled the situation well, viewers should “give a bit of grace to Mariella, and everyone in the camp”.
He said: “[It is] a really weird situation that every single person’s in, and I’m not sure if people go at stuff with the clearest head. You get these weird breakdowns and I think that’s what we’re seeing.”
An ITV statement said: “The production monitors everyone in camp 24/7 and if at any time we feel someone has overstepped the line by using inappropriate language or displaying unacceptable behaviour, we would take steps to intervene and speak to everyone involved.
“The duty of care for our contestants is of the utmost importance to us. We take the welfare of the celebrities very seriously and have measures in place to ensure they are supported at every stage of the process: before, during and after filming.”

President Cyril Ramaphosa has faced calls to resign over his handling of the "Farmgate" scandal
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa has won a legal battle to overturn a report that found he may have a case to answer over the theft of large sums of cash from his private farm.
In 2022, an independent panel said Ramaphosa may have committed serious misconduct relating to the theft of $580,000 (£443,000), hidden in a sofa, at his Phala Phala game farm in the Limpopo province. He denied any wrongdoing.
Ramaphosa challenged the findings of the report in court after the Constitutional Court ruled that parliament had violated the constitution by blocking moves to impeach him.
The Western Cape high court ruled that the panel's report was unlawful and set it aside "in its entirety".
In its judgment, the court said the panel, appointed by parliament to investigate the allegations against Ramaphosa, had "misconstrued its function, the nature of the inquiry it was to conduct and the recommendation it was required to make".
"It went beyond its lawful remit ... and made several material errors of law. [Therefore] the report of the independent panel ... is declared unlawful and is reviewed and set aside in its entirety," Judge Nolwazi Mabindla-Boqwana said.
The court also declared unlawful the steps taken by parliament in relation to the report.
Political analyst Khanyi Magubane said the court ruling was a victory for Ramaphosa as it gave him "political and constitutional credibility".
She made it clear that the ruling was not a criminal finding on possible improper conduct at the farm but rather an indictment at the independent panel's report.
"[So] he does get significant reprieve ... but there will always be the shadow of the Phala Phala report," Magubane said.
The ruling effectively removes the basis for the parliamentary impeachment process against Ramaphosa, although opposition parties have indicated they intend to challenge the decision.
The scandal, dubbed "Farmgate" by local media, has has dogged Ramaphosa since it emerged in 2022, when former spy chief Arthur Fraser reported the matter to police in a dossier.
Fraser, an ally of former President Jacob Zuma, accused Ramaphosa of concealing the theft from the police and tax authorities.
The break-in took place in 2020, when thieves allegedly stole bundles of US dollar bills hidden inside a sofa at the farm.
Opposition parties, pictured above, have been vocal in their call for the president to account for his role in the saga
Earlier this month, two people were found guilty of the theft.
Ramaphosa confirmed that a robbery had taken place but said the money had been from the legitimate sale of buffalo from his livestock business.
Several investigations cleared him of any wrongdoing, but parliament began an impeachment proceedings in 2022 and appointed an independent panel to investigate the allegations.
The panel made a series of damaging findings, including that there was "substantial doubt about the legitimacy of the source of the currency that was stolen".
Ramaphosa initially challenged the report in court but withdrew his application after parliament voted against adopting its findings.
He revived the legal challenge again in May this year after the Constitutional Court, the country's highest court , ruled that parliament had acted unconstitutionally by blocking moves to impeach him.
It ordered parliament to refer the report to an impeachment committee.
In his latest challenge, Ramaphosa argued that the panel had "misconceived its mandate, misjudged the information placed before it and misinterpreted the four charges advanced against me".
The Western Cape High Court's ruling could bring the current impeachment process to an end, unless parliament successfully challenges the decision.
If they do, and the appeal is successful, the parliamentary committee would be able to examine the charges against the president and make a recommendation.
If the committee recommends impeachment, parliament would have to vote on whether to remove him from office. This would require the support of at least two-thirds majority in parliament.
Ramaphosa's Africa National Congress (ANC) has enough parliamentary seats to block such a move.
He is the first president to face impeachment proceedings under the rules introduced in 2018.
Legal expert Professor Richard Calland told the BBC he had expected the court ruling, given what he termed as "fault lines" in the independent panel's report.
Calland said the court's findings now meant that the impeachment process was "dead in the water [and] cannot continue".
He said that any political party that wanted to revive it "would have to come up with a whole new basis" for this.
Calland said political parties who want to hold Ramaphosa accountable would likely seek to appeal the ruling but it was unlikely parliament would also do so.
"So, the president's political career is now free of the cloud of impeachment," he said.

The ruling hands the president ​a political reprieve by removing a finding that had exposed him to possible impeachment.
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa has won a court bid challenging an independent panel’s report that had paved the way for his possible impeachment over misconduct allegations linked to a burglary-turned-political scandal called “Farmgate”.
The Western Cape High Court on Wednesday declared unlawful the 2022 findings of an independent parliamentary panel that accused Ramaphosa of a conflict of interest over the origin of large amounts of cash stolen from a sofa at his ranch in 2020.
The ruling hands Ramaphosa a political reprieve by removing a finding that had exposed him to possible impeachment at a vulnerable moment for him and his African National Congress (ANC) party.
“The court found that the panel fundamentally misconstrued its functions,” Judge Nolwazi Mabindla-Boqwana said, reading the court’s unanimous decision.
“The ‌panel went beyond its lawful remit, asked itself wrong questions and made several material errors of law.”
Ramaphosa “notes” and “will study” the court’s judgement relating to his Phala Phala game farm, the president’s office said in a statement.
“In seeking the judicial review, President Ramaphosa exercised a constitutional right,” the statement read. “In line with his respect for the rule of law including judicial independence, President Ramaphosa will study the decision of the court.”
The theft came to light after a former intelligence boss reported to the police that Ramaphosa had allegedly sought to cover up a theft of millions of US dollars in cash at his farm, initially claiming it was about $4m.
Ramaphosa has always denied wrongdoing and said the $580,000 stolen at his farm ⁠was money from the sale of buffaloes.
But the episode raised questions about ⁠why he had so much cash stuffed in furniture.
The 2022 report said the president failed to report the theft through proper channels, violated the constitution regarding paid work from his farm and directed presidential security to do police work.
The African Transformation Movement party, which is in favour of Ramaphosa’s impeachment, criticised the ruling.
The matter has been embarrassing for a ⁠leader who came to power promising to fight corruption and clean up the image of the former liberation movement.
The ANC won about 31 percent of the vote in this month’s local elections, its worst-ever such result, extending a decline that saw it lose its national parliamentary majority in 2024 for the first time since the end of apartheid and beginning of democracy.
The Constitutional Court revived impeachment proceedings against the president in ⁠May.
It found that a 2022 parliamentary vote to stop the process ⁠was invalid and parliament should set up an impeachment inquiry.
The Western Cape High Court in July temporarily halted the inquiry pending the outcome of Wednesday’s ruling.
Ramaphosa, 74, has been head of state since 2018, and his second presidential ‌term ‌is to end in 2029. The ANC is due to elect its next leader next year when Ramaphosa will step down after two five-year terms as party leader.

Raheem Sterling has avoided being sent to jail after he received a suspended sentence of 12 months for pleading guilty to a prolonged period of reckless driving while impaired by the drug nitrous oxide.
The former England international, who five years ago was leading the Three Lions’ charge to a European Championship final, stood expressionless in the dock as the sentence was read out by district judge Kirsty Allman at Basingstoke magistrates court.
Sterling was sentenced to 18 months in prison, reduced to 12 months, for dangerous driving on the morning of 28 May this year. He was awarded a sentence of two months for a failure to provide a specimen of blood for analysis, which is to run concurrently. He received no punishment for possession of a class C drug. Canisters in Sterling’s possession were seized and destroyed.
In sentencing, Allman found the first two offences to be of the highest levels of culpability but argued that Sterling’s charitable work, and his award of an MBE in 2021, acted as “significant and substantial” mitigation. Sterling was also commended for having voluntary submitted to addiction treatment, spending 12 days at the Banbury Lodge addiction treatment centre in June. Under the sentencing act of 2026, there is a presumption that any custodial sentence of 12 months or less be suspended.
Sterling must complete 100 hours of community service and has been banned from driving for 24 months.
Sterling was first observed behaving erratically at 1.30am on 28 May, when he was spotted inhaling from a large pink balloon while behind the wheel of his black Lamborghini Urus outside McDonald’s in Hayes. After a night without sleep, Sterling got behind the wheel again at 7.45am. Four police forces received reports concerning Sterling’s driving along the M25, M40 and M3, with one witness describing it as “absolutely horrendous”. Forced to overtake, the witness saw Sterling inhaling from a large white balloon.
On leaving the M3, the Lamborghini veered off the carriageway on the A327, crashing into the central reservation and causing “substantial damage” to the vehicle which “was no longer drivable”, according to Allman’s sentencing remarks.
Sterling complied with initial roadside breath and saliva tests, which proved negative for alcohol, cannabis and cocaine. At Basingstoke police station Sterling admitted he “had a problem with nitrous oxide” and went on to fail a preliminary impairment test. He was also asked to judge 30 seconds with his eyes closed but recorded 52. Sterling then refused to give a blood sample for further testing until he was accompanied by a lawyer.
Allman said the nature of the offences were such that she had considered the possibility of passing sentencing on to a crown court. “These offences are so serious that neither a fine nor a community order can be justified,” she said. “The custodial threshold is clearly crossed, and custody is unavoidable.”
Custody was avoided, however, after Allman took into consideration Sterling’s receipt of an MBE for services to racial equality in sport in 2021 and his ongoing commitment both to the Raheem Sterling foundation and the RS7 football academy. “I attach substantial weight to your personal mitigation,” she said.
In the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.
If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.
If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from the iOS App Store on iPhone or the Google Play store on Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.
“I further accept that nitrous oxide became a maladaptive coping mechanism during a difficult period in your career,” Allman went on. At the time of his arrest, Sterling had just completed an unsuccessful period at Feyenoord, having spent the previous six months training alone, excluded from Chelsea’s first team.
Speaking for the defence, Jason Bartfeld KC, described the incident as “extremely sad” and said for Sterling it was “a matter of his own intense personal regret” which had “tarnished his personal reputation”. Sterling left the court without making comment.

Budget retail chain expected to be broken up, with store closures, after US owner rejected at least two last-ditch bids
Poundland has collapsed into administration, putting more than 10,000 jobs at risk in “devastating news” for staff in the run-up to Christmas.
Administrators at AlixPartners have been appointed to the retailer, which has 600 stores in the UK and Ireland, by Poundland’s directors. The chain is now expected to be broken up, with significant job losses and store closures after its owners rejected at least two last-ditch bids for the budget retailer.
AlixPartners said a sales process “did not identify a viable solvent solution for the business as a whole”. It said Poundland employed more than 10,000 people, which the Guardian understands is about 2,000 fewer than were in the business just a month ago.
It has been suggested that as many as 30,000 jobs in total could be at risk in Poundland’s stores, supply chain and at other affected businesses on high streets around the country.
Poundland would continue to trade with all stores and distribution centres remaining open while administrators pursued “all options including sales of the business and its assets, either in whole or part, from administration”, AlixPartners said.
Bally Auluk, a national officer for shopworkers’ union Usdaw, said: “This is devastating news for our members, who were only recently praised by management for helping to turn the business around.
“There is never a good time for this to happen, but just before Christmas has to be the worst. This decision has been made by the owners, Gordon Brothers, despite failing to engage with Usdaw, which is a disgraceful way to treat our members.”
The US finance firm, which bought Poundland for a nominal £1 from the European retail group Pepco last year, has been under pressure to accept an offer that would save jobs and protect thousands of the retailer’s suppliers.
Gordon Brothers said on Wednesday afternoon it had “explored every avenue to secure a sale of the whole company” but that Poundland was “still vulnerable to inflationary pressures or any downturn in sales and margin”.
It said: “Poundland has faced several years of instability. In July 2025, Gordon Brothers supported the company’s restructuring plan – stepping in when no one else was willing to finance the business.”
In notes seen by the Guardian, Poundland’s directors wrote to staff and suppliers on Wednesday expressing “sincere sadness and intense regret” that they had been forced to call in administrators after Gordon Brothers said it would not provide more funds to keep the business operating as there was “no prospect of an acceptable solvent offer”.
Poundland’s managing director, Barry Williams, told suppliers: “We know this outcome will be as disappointing to you as it is to us.” About 2,000 suppliers will lose significant business and millions of pounds in payments for stock already supplied.
High inflation and heavy competition from budget stores, online specialists and supermarkets have left the 36-year-old retail chain – the UK’s first and biggest nationwide single-price retailer – struggling.
Poundland’s board filed a notice of intention to appoint administrations last month – which was later extended – protecting the retailer from the demands of creditors until 26 November while a solution to its problems was sought.
Just two bidders interested in the whole company remained in talks right up until this week’s deadline.
Martin Property Group, a Northern Ireland family-owned company, which has been working with the existing management for about two months, remained interested.
It was joined by a last-ditch bid from Germany’s Zachert Private Equity, a fund founded by a former Bloomberg journalist that specialises in acquiring mid-sized companies.
Other bidders for the whole group included the little-known finance group Xyra Group Holdings, and the Irish investment company Innovest, which both fell out of the bidding race over the past week.
AlixPartners said: “We would encourage anybody interested in acquiring the business in part or as a whole, as well as UK retail operators with open employment opportunities, to contact the administrators.”
Poundland’s board was forced to appoint administrators before Thursday’s deadline as shelves began to empty because the company was running short of funds to restock during its peak Christmas trading period.
Gordon Brothers’ UK director, Mark Newton-Jones, held the latest of several meetings with the business secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, on Monday, more than a week after giving evidence to the business select committee. MPs called on the government to protect Poundland and other high street stores from “predatory capitalism” and asset-stripping last week.
Andy Burnham, the prime minister, said: “Poundland is a part of the fabric of high streets across the country and the news it has gone into administration just weeks before Christmas will be deeply concerning for workers and their families. We will make every effort to secure a deal that protects jobs and keeps as many shops open as possible.”
MPs have accused the Poundland owner of extracting millions of pounds from the retailer when it was on a “knife-edge”.
Documents provided to MPs showed the finance firm had taken close to £20m in interest payments and various fees, including those relating to store closures since acquiring Poundland.
Liam Byrne, the Labour chair of the business select committee, said he had recalled Newton-Jones to give public evidence. He said the committee was seeking assurances that Gordon Brothers or any related party would not act in any “insolvency capacity in relation to Poundland”.
Poundland, which was founded with one store in Burton upon Trent in 1990, has endured a rocky history under a string of different owners as it has faced rising costs and heavy competition from chains such as Savers, Home Bargains and B&M, as well as from the big supermarkets. Poundland co-founder Steve Smith said he was “gutted” about the chain’s administration.
It is now expected to be broken up with retailers such as Poundstretcher, B&M and The Range taking parcels of stores but leaving potentially hundreds empty.
Gordon Brothers rejected an initial management-backed rescue bid financed by Martin Property Group for the discount chain.
The US-based finance company said it could raise more from a breakup of Poundland – selling off stock and parcels of stores to rival retailers – than through the solvent bids. Those bids promised only a small upfront payment for the £30m in shareholder debts that Gordon Brothers took on with its fellow shareholder – Poundland’s former owner Pepco – at the time of buying the chain.

The Salvadoran national’s lawyer said in a statement that it was ‘a temporary departure’.
Kilmar Abrego Garcia relieved to not be arrested after US court hearing
Kilmar Abrego Garcia, a Salvadoran national whose wrongful deportation to El ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Salvador drew sharp criticism of United States President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown, has arrived in Spain.
Abrego Garcia did not speak to reporters as he arrived at Madrid’s main international airport on Wednesday, but raised a fist as he climbed into a van.
He voluntarily departed the US a day earlier after months of legal opposition to a second deportation, this time to one of various African countries proposed by Department of Homeland Security (DHS) officials. A judge had told him to self-deport by Tuesday, The Associated Press news agency reported, citing a source familiar with the matter.
In a post on X, the DHS said: “It’s not surprising this criminal illegal alien would choose to go to Spain, a country that earlier this year was invaded by tens of thousands of illegal aliens … Good riddance.”
Abrego Garcia’s lawyer, Simon Sandoval-Moshenberg, described the move as “a temporary departure”.
“Mr Abrego Garcia has many options to return to the United States as the husband of a US citizen spouse and the father of a US citizen child. We don’t expect that to happen under this administration,” he said in a statement.
Sandoval-Moshenberg noted the US government had sought to deport Garcia “in shackles on an ICE Air flight to Liberia”.
US Senator Chris Van Hollen, a Democrat from Maryland, the state where Abrego Garcia ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠lived with his family for around a decade before being deported, said the Trump administration “was forced to come to this agreement that respects Kilmar’s will.”
The departure of Abrego Garcia, 31, brings an end to a legal fight that, at one point, reached the US ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Supreme Court.
US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrested Abrego Garcia in Baltimore in March 2025. He was then transferred to a megaprison in El Salvador despite a prior court order barring him from being sent to the country because of the risk of persecution.
A US official later called the transfer an “administrative error”.
After the Supreme Court ordered the government to facilitate Garcia’s return, prosecutors secured a criminal indictment charging him with human smuggling in a case stemming from an earlier incident. The Trump administration then brought him back ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠to the US in June 2025. It later tried to deport him to Liberia ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠after a US judge dismissed the human smuggling charge.

Pop müziğin sevilen sesi Derya Uluğ, yaklaşık 10 yıldır birlikte olduğu müzisyen Asil Gök ile evlenmeye hazırlanıyor. Kenan İmirzalıoğlu, Burak Hakkı ve Atilla Saral, yıllar önce aynı podyumlarda yer aldıkları eski arkadaşları Murat Mısırlı'yı evinde ziyaret etti. Yaklaşık yedi yıl önce ALS teşhisi konan Mısırlı'nın dostlarıyla bir araya geldiği anlar, Atilla Saral'ın paylaşımıyla kısa sürede sosyal medyada ilgi çekti. Uzun süredir gözlerden uzak bir hayat süren eski mankenin bu buluşmada yalnız bırakılmaması ise ziyaretin en çok konuşulan yanı oldu. Ziyaretin amacı, haberlere göre eski dostuna moral vermekti.
1968'de İzmir 'in Karşıyaka ilçesinde dünyaya gelen Murat Mısırlı, İstanbul Üniversitesi'nde mühendislik okurken modelliğe adım attı ve kısa sürede 1990'lı yılların tanınan podyum isimlerinden biri oldu. Haberlere göre Türkiye'yi 30 farklı ülkede temsil eden Mısırlı, modellik kariyerinin yanında Sait Sökmen'den dans eğitimi aldı, Levent Kırca Tiyatrosu'nda sahne deneyimi yaşadı ve çeşitli televizyon dizilerinde rol aldı. Kariyerindeki bu çok yönlülük, onu yalnızca podyumda değil sahnede ve ekranda da tanınan bir isim haline getirdi. 2006'da tanıştığı yogayı zamanla mesleğine dönüştüren Mısırlı, Hatha Yoga eğitmenliği yapmaya başladı.
Bu hareketli hayat, yaklaşık yedi yıl önce konan ve motor nöronları etkileyerek zamanla kas gücünün azalmasına yol açan amyotrofik lateral skleroz, yani ALS teşhisiyle podyumlardan ve ekranlardan uzak, sakin bir düzene dönüştü; Mısırlı mücadelesini bugün evinde sürdürüyor. Haziran ayındaki 58. yaş gününde eşi Burcu Ergün Mısırlı ve oğlu Tibet ile Arzum Onan ve Uğurkan Erez gibi yakın dostları onu sürprizle karşılamış, o kutlamanın fotoğrafları da sosyal medyada yer almıştı.
Mısırlı'nın etrafındaki bu yakın çevreye kasım ayında eski model arkadaşları Kenan İmirzalıoğlu, Atilla Saral ve Burak Hakkı da katıldı. Sabah'ın aktardığına göre üç isim, eski dostlarına moral vermek için evinde bir araya geldi, uzun süre sohbet etti ve Mısırlı'nın etrafında toplanıp sarılarak fotoğraf çektirdi. Bu kareleri sosyal medya hesabından paylaşan isim Atilla Saral oldu ve paylaşımına 'Can arkadaşlar' notunu düştü.
Paylaşılan karelerden birinde Mısırlı, kırmızı-siyah kareli gömleğiyle ön sırada dostlarının arasında gülümserken görülüyor; bir diğerinde ise geniş bir sofranın etrafında toplanan kalabalık bir grup dikkat çekiyor. Yıllar sonra bir araya gelen eski podyum arkadaşlarının bu buluşması, paylaşılan fotoğraflarla birlikte sosyal medyada ilgi gördü.

Raheem Sterling pleaded guilty at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court in September and admitted possession of six nitrous oxide cannisters for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Former England player Raheem Sterling has been given a suspended 12-month jail sentence for dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide after a crash involving a Lamborghini on the motorway.
Sterling pleaded guilty at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court in September to driving a Lamborghini Urus dangerously on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road before he crashed on May 28. The sentence is suspended for 18 months.
He has also been handed a two-year driving ban and must undertake 100 hours of unpaid community work. Sterling will have to re-take a driving test to hold a licence.
The 31-year-old admitted possession of six nitrous oxide cannisters for wrongful inhalation, a class C drug, and failing to provide a specimen.
Mitigating factors taken into account by District Judge Kirsty Allman were Sterling's guilty plea, that he had no prior convictions and a clean driving licence prior to his arrest in May.
She also said she took into account Sterling's regret at his behaviour, attached great weight to testimonies about his character and the fact that, away from his footballing career and perhaps not in the public sphere, he is heavily involved with several charitable causes from the Raheem Sterling Foundation, the RS7 Academy and several charitable bursaries.
Further mitigation was that Sterling engaged with addiction services soon after his arrest in May and admitted himself into residential care for 12 days at an addiction centre, which the court saw as "genuine engagement".
The judge said Sterling was entirely culpable for the dangerous driving charge, saying: "You chose to drive, disregarding the safety of others".
Chief Inspector Chris Sharland from Hampshire Police said: "Nitrous oxide, commonly known as laughing gas or NOS, is a Class C drug, and driving whilst under its influence is an emerging threat to the safety of motorists on our roads.
"Driving whilst impaired with nitrous oxide can cause unconsciousness, and in the worst-case scenarios neurological damage or death, so there is a very real risk of causing serious harm to yourself or other motorists.
"We urge drivers to be aware of not only the law, but the risk this type of behaviour carries - one decision can have devastating consequences."
Sterling scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, helping Gareth Southgate's side reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and the final of Euro 2020. He came through the academy at QPR before joining Liverpool, where he made his senior debut.
Sterling, who was born in Kingston, Jamaica, moved to Manchester City in 2015 and won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup in 2019. He left for Chelsea in 2022 but after falling out of favour spent the 2024/25 season on loan at Arsenal.
Sterling joined Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term deal until the end of the 2025/26 season. He is currently without a club.
In the 2021 Queen's Birthday Honours, Sterling was made an MBE for services to racial equality in sport after fronting anti-racism and discrimination campaigns and speaking out strongly against racism on and off the pitch for several years.
It came amid controversy over England fans booing players taking the knee at matches as a gesture against intolerance.
Sky Sports News' Geraint Hughes at Basingstoke Magistrates Court:
"When Raheem Sterling arrived at Basingstoke Magistrates Court for his sentencing, as you would expect he looked serious, but also quite anxious.
"He was wearing dark clothing and never once did his gaze do anything other than look forward or towards the judge inside the courtroom. You felt he was aware of the gravity of the situation and also - given that his legal team had told the court how ashamed he felt to be in this position and that he never ever wanted to be in front of a criminal court in his life again - you could sense that with his body language and his demeanour.
"When the district judge asked Raheem Sterling to stand while she delivered her sentence he did so at times looking downwards, but mainly straight at the judge, occasionally acknowledging her remarks.
"At the conclusion of her sentencing, when Sterling was told he was free to leave the court, there was no smile or any emotion. He just walked out of the courtroom with his legal team to whom he shook their hands and thanked them very quietly before being able to leave the court a free man having avoided a potential custodial sentence."

İstanbul Valiliği'nin duyurusuna göre M2 Yenikapı-Hacıosman metro hattının Taksim istasyonu ile F1 Taksim-Kabataş füniküler hattı bugün saat 15.00 itibarıyla işletmeye kapatılıyor. Kapanışın ne kadar süreceği henüz belli değil; Valilik, iki hattın da 'ikinci bir duyuruya kadar' kapalı kalacağını bildirdi.
Metro İstanbul'un paylaşımına göre M2 hattında seferler sürecek, ancak trenler Taksim istasyonunda durmadan geçecek. Füniküler hattında ise yolcu taşınmayacak. Taksim'e gitmek isteyenlerin Şişhane ya da Osmanbey istasyonlarını kullanması gerekecek.
Şişhane istasyonunda da kısmi bir kısıtlama var: İstiklal Caddesi ve Beyoğlu Belediyesi 6. Daire çıkışları yolcular tarafından kullanılamayacak. Valilik, yolcuların istasyonun diğer giriş-çıkışlarından yararlanabileceğini belirtti.

Bu nedenle bugün saat 14.00'ten etkinlik bitimine kadar Taksim çevresindeki bazı yollar ulaşıma kapatılacak. Kapatılan güzergâhlar arasında Sıraselviler Caddesi'nin Hocazade Sokak kesişiminden Taksim Meydanı yönüne giden bölümü, Taksim Meydanı'nda büfelerin önünden İstiklal Caddesi'ne bağlanan yol, Refik Saydam Caddesi üzerinden Asmalımescit Caddesi'ne giriş ve çıkışlar ile Taksim Tüneli girişinden İstiklal yönüne giden yol var.
Yeni Çarşı Caddesi, Kumbaracı Yokuşu, Turnacıbaşı Caddesi, Meşelik Sokak ve Sadrialışık Sokak'tan İstiklal Caddesi yönüne giden yollar da trafiğe kapalı olacak. Tak-ı Zafer Caddesi ile Mete Caddesi'nin Önünü Caddesi kesişiminden itibaren olan bölümü de aynı kapsamda. Sürücülere alternatif olarak Önünü Caddesi, Tarlabaşı Bulvarı, Refik Saydam Caddesi ve Meclis-i Mebusan Caddesi öneriliyor.

Olay, 21 Kasım’da İzmit ilçesi Yeşilova Mahallesi'nde meydana geldi. Kız çocuğunun sokakta sürdüğü bisiklet, yol kenarında duran otomobile sürttü.
Durumu fark edip otomobilden inen erkek sürücü, kızın bisikletini aldı. Çocuğa bağıran ismi öğrenilemeyen sürücü, ailesini çağırmasını istedi.
Çevredekilerin ve esnafın uyarılarına rağmen tepkisini sürdüren sürücüden korkan kız, annesine haber vermek için eve gitti. Bu sırada otomobilden inen ve sürücünün annesi olduğu öğrenilen kadın, çocuğun bisikletini birkaç kez kaldırıp yere vurarak kırdı.
Daha sonra kız çocuğu da annesiyle olay yerine gelince taraflar arasında tartışma çıktı.
Yaşananlar, bir iş yerinin güvenlik kamerasına yansıdı. Görüntülerin haberleştirilmesinin ardından kimliklerini belirlenen anne ve oğlunun polis merkezinde ifadeleri alındı. Anne-oğul daha sonra serbest bırakıldı. Tarafların birbirinden şikayetçi olmadıkları belirtildi.
Olayı haberlerden gören ve kızın dedesi Nazmi Sağlam ile buluşan şarkıcı Demet Akalın , sanal medya hesabından kız çocuğuna yeni bir bisiklet hediye ettiğini açıkladı.
Sağlam ile birlikte çektiği videoyu da sanal medya hesabından paylaşan Akalın, "Geldim kızı buldum. Şimdi bisikleti almaya gidiyoruz" dedi.

15 Temmuz hain darbe girişiminde Türkiye'nin bağımsızlığı ve milli iradesi için canlarını feda eden kahramanların aileleri, Antalya 'da düzenlenen 10. Şehit Aileleri Buluşması'nda bir araya geldi. 15 Temmuz Derneği tarafından gerçekleştirilen programda şehit yakınları, aradan geçen yıllara rağmen taşıdıkları acıyı, gururu ve vatan sevgisini Sabah'tan Barış Savaş'la paylaştı.
"Hep Sen Varsın Diye" temasıyla gerçekleştirilen buluşmada, şehit aileleri arasındaki dayanışma ve kardeşlik ruhu ön plana çıktı. Etkinliğe katılan İçişleri Bakan Yardımcısı Bülent Turan da ailelerle sohbet ederek şehit yakınları ve gazilerle bir arada olmaktan onur duyduğunu ifade etti.
15 Temmuz Derneği'nin şehit yakınlarını yalnız bırakmamak ve darbe girişimini unutturmamak amacıyla yürüttüğü çalışmalara dikkat çeken Bülent Turan, darbeciler ile demokrasi ve milletin yanında duranlar arasında net bir tercih bulunduğunu söyledi.
Turan, "Ya darbecinin yanındasınız ya da demokrasinin, milletin yanındasınız. Ama o darbeciler o hastalığı aldığı zaman kanser hücresi gibi ne zaman fırsat bulsalar bir yerden patlıyor, kendini gösteriyor" ifadelerini kullandı.
Şehitlerin milli iradenin ve demokrasinin korunması için büyük bedel ödediğini vurgulayan Turan, "Evlatlarınız bu ülkede milli irade devam etsin diye, sistem, demokrasi çalışsın diye bedel ödedi. Tekrar tekrar darbe çığırtkanlığı yapmanın bu ülkeye hiçbir faydası yok. Hiçbir darbeden sonra ekonomimizin büyümediğini, siyasetin büyümediğini, ülkemizin büyümediğini yaşayarak gördük. O yüzden demokrasi içerisinde, milli iradenin hakimiyetinde yolumuza devam edeceğiz" dedi.
Toplumsal huzur ve kardeşliğin korunmasının önemine de değinen Turan, "Ne olursa olsun umutsuz olmayacağız. Ne olursa olsun sorunlarımızı aşacağımıza, 86 milyonun kardeşliğiyle beraber aşacağımıza inanarak yola devam edeceğiz" diye konuştu.
15 Temmuz Derneği Başkanı İsmail Hakkı Turunç, yaptığı açıklamada darbe girişiminin uluslararası alanda anlatılması için yürüttükleri çalışmaları anlattı.
Dışişleri Bakanlığı, TİKA, Türkiye Maarif Vakfı ve Yunus Emre Enstitüsü ile ortak programlar gerçekleştirdiklerini belirten Turunç, bugüne kadar 61 ülkeyi ziyaret ederek 15 Temmuz'un perde arkasını anlattıklarını söyledi. Şehit ve gazi çocuklarına yönelik eğitim ve istihdam desteklerinin sürdüğünü de aktaran Turunç, şehit aileleri arasındaki güçlü dayanışmaya dikkat çekti.
Turunç, "Şehit ailelerinin çoğu zaman maddi bir talepten ziyade hatırlanmaya ihtiyacı var. Bir şehit babasını başka bir şehit babası can kulağıyla dinler. Bir şehit annesi başka bir şehit annesini yüzündeki tebessümden, ses tonundan anlar. Aralarında çok güçlü bir kardeşlik ruhu oluştu" ifadelerini kullandı.
15 Temmuz darbe girişiminin başarılı olması halinde Türkiye'nin büyük bir iç savaşa sürükleneceğini belirten Turunç, Başkan Recep Tayyip Erdoğan'ın kararlı tutumu ve milletin meydanlara inmesiyle emperyal planların bozulduğunu kaydetti. Turunç, milli direnişin 11'inci yılında şehit ailelerini kutsal topraklara götürmek için çalışmalar yürüttüklerini de bildirdi.
15 Temmuz gecesi darbe girişiminin seyrini değiştiren kahraman Astsubay Ömer Halisdemir 'in ailesi de buluşmada gurur dolu anlar yaşadı. Şehidin kızı Teğmen Elif Nur Halisdemir, babasının izinden giderek Özel Kuvvetler Komutanlığı bünyesinde bordo bereli oldu.
Şehidin babası Hasan Hüseyin Halisdemir, torununun asker olmasından duyduğu mutluluğu dile getirirken vatan sevgisini şu sözlerle anlattı:
"Üç tane oğlum kaldı. Torunlarım, Ömerlerim var, onları da yetiştiriyorum. Onları da vatana hibe ederim."
Ömer Halisdemir'in kardeşi Soner Halisdemir, ağabeyinin mirasının yeni nesiller tarafından yaşatıldığını belirtti. Şehidin naaşı baba ocağına geldiğinde bordo beresini kızının aldığını ve giydiğini anlatan Soner Halisdemir, yeğeninin bugün de babasının izinden yürüdüğünü söyledi.
Soner Halisdemir, "Bugün Ömer olur, yarın Fatih olur, yarın Ali olur. Bizde Ömerler hiç bitmez. Söz konusu vatan ve milletse 30 kurşun olsa ne yazar, 30 bin kurşun olsa ne yazar? Biz unutmadık, unutturmayacağız" dedi.
Ankara Gölbaşı Özel Harekat Daire Başkanlığı'na düzenlenen saldırıda ikiz polis memuru oğulları Ahmet ve Mehmet Oruç'u şehit veren baba Hacı Ali Oruç da yaşadıklarını paylaştı.
Henüz stajyer olan ve görevleri resmen başlamayan oğullarının, amirlerinin "Gelmeyin" uyarısına rağmen 15 Temmuz gecesi mücadeleye katıldığını anlatan Oruç, ikizlerin "Biz de bu personelin içindeyiz, elimizden geldiği kadar yardımcı olmak istiyoruz" diyerek görev yerlerine gittiklerini aktardı.
Oğullarının helikopterleri hangardan çıkarırken atılan ilk bombayla şehit düştüğünü belirten Hacı Ali Oruç, acı haberi sabah saatlerinde önce Ahmet'in, ardından Mehmet'in şehadetiyle aldığını söyledi.
İki evladını aynı gece kaybeden baba, yaşadığı büyük acıya rağmen gururunu şu sözlerle dile getirdi:
"İki evlat vermek kolay değil; acısı da büyük, makamı da büyük. Cenab-ı Allah bizi bu makama layık gördüyse ne mutlu bize. Her babaya, her anneye nasip olmaz. Oğullarımızla gururlanıyoruz."
15 Temmuz gecesi Türkiye'nin bağımsızlığı için mücadele edenler arasında Türk vatandaşlarının yanı sıra Türkiye'ye gönül veren yabancılar da yer aldı. İstanbul'da çalışan Fas uyruklu Cevad Merrun, Başkan Recep Tayyip Erdoğan'ın çağrısını televizyondan duyduktan sonra arkadaşlarının "Sen misafirimizsin, dışarı çıkma" uyarılarına rağmen sokağa çıktı. Türkiye için tankların karşısına dikilen Merrun, darbe girişimi sırasında şehit düştü.
Ağabeyinin şehadet haberini sabah saat 06.00'da aldıklarını anlatan Selahaddin Merrun, yaşadıkları acıyı ve gururu şu sözlerle aktardı:
"İlk aldığımız haberle yıkıldık ama şehit olduğunu öğrenince büyük bir gurur duyduk. Ağabeyim Recep Tayyip Erdoğan'ı ve Türkiye'yi çok seviyordu. Aradan yıllar geçse de onu hiç aklımdan çıkaramıyorum. Ağabeyimle çok gurur duyuyorum."

Eski model Murat Mısırlı, yaklaşık 7 yıldır ALS hastalığıyla mücadele ediyor. Mısırlı'yı bu süreçte dostları yalnız bırakmıyor. Bir dönem mankenlik de yapan oyuncular; Kenan İmirzalıoğlu , Atilla Saral ve Burak Hakkı, Mısırlı'yı ziyaret etti. Yıllara dayanan arkadaşlığın buluşmasından fotoğraflar sosyal medyada paylaşıldı. Atilla Saral, fotoğrafa "Can arkadaşlar" notunu ekledi.
Murat Mısırlı, 1968 yılında İzmir'in Karşıyaka ilçesinde doğdu. İlkokul yıllarından itibaren sporla ilgilenen Mısırlı, gençliğinde tenis, judo ve hentbol dallarında amatör ve profesyonel olarak faaliyet gösterdi. İstanbul Üniversitesi'nde mühendislik eğitimi aldığı sırada gelen modellik tekliflerini değerlendiren Mısırlı, 1990'lı yıllarda Türkiye'nin tanınmış erkek mankenlerinden biri oldu.
Mısırlı, profesyonel dansçılık da yaptı. Yurt dışında düzenlenen organizasyonlarda Türkiye'yi 30 farklı ülkede temsil etti. Güzellik yarışmalarının ve defilelerin koreografi çalışmalarında görev aldı. Oyunculuk kariyerine de adım atan Murat Mısırlı, Levent Kırca Tiyatrosu'nda sahneye çıktı ve çeşitli televizyon dizilerinde rol aldı. Burcu Ergün Mısırlı ile evli olan eski mankenin Tibet adında bir oğlu bulunuyor.
Amyotrofik lateral skleroz ya da ALS, esas olarak istemli kas hareketinin kontrolünden sorumlu sinir hücrelerinin hasarından kaynaklanan nadir bir nörolojik hastalık grubudur. İstemli kaslar çiğneme, yürüme ve konuşma gibi hareketlerin yapılmasında görevlidir. ALS hastalığı ilerleyicidir ve belirtiler zamanla kötüleşme eğilimi gösterir. Günümüzde, ALS hastalığının ilerleyişini durdurmak ya da tam tedavi sağlamak için herhangi bir tedavi seçeneği yoktur ancak bu konudaki araştırmalar devam etmektedir.

Törenin saat 20.00'de başlaması bekleniyor. Uluğ'un gece boyunca tek bir gelinlikle yetinmeyeceği, birden fazla gelinlik giyeceği öğrenildi. Düğüne çiftin aileleri ve yakınlarının yanında magazin dünyasından ünlü isimlerin de katılması bekleniyor.
"Canavar", "Okyanus" ve "Kanunlar Gibi" şarkılarıyla tanınan 40 yaşındaki Derya Uluğ, evlilik teklifini bu yılın şubat ayında, kendi doğum gününde aldı. Şarkıcı o günü sosyal medya hesabından "I Said Yes!" notuyla duyurmuştu. Çift haziran ayında nişanlandı. Uluğ nişan törenini "Çok tatlı, sade, tam istediğimiz gibi gönlümüze göre güzel bir gün oldu" sözleriyle anlatmıştı.

Bu yıl 10'uncusu düzenlenen Geleneksel Şehit Aileleri Buluşması, Antalya'nın Kemer ilçesindeki bir otelde gerçekleşti. Geceye Gençlik ve Spor Bakan Yardımcısı Enes Eminoğlu, Aile ve Sosyal Hizmetler Bakan Yardımcısı Zafer Tarıkdaroğlu, Antalya Valisi Hulusi Şahin, Kemer Kaymakamı Ahmet Solmaz, Kepez Kaymakamı Suat Dervişoğlu, 15 Temmuz Derneği Başkanı İsmail Hakkı Turunç, şehit yakınları ve protokol üyeleri katıldı.
Aile ve Sosyal Hizmetler Bakan Yardımcısı Zafer Tarıkdaroğlu, aynı çatı altında, aynı gönül bağı ile bir araya gelmenin mutluluğunu yaşadıklarını belirterek, 15 Temmuz gecesinde gösterilen iradenin ülkenin kaderini yeniden yazdığını söyledi.
Tarıkdaroğlu, "15 Temmuz gecesi aziz milletimizin demokrasisine, bağımsızlığına ve geleceğine nasıl sahip çıktığını tüm dünyaya göstermiş olduğu bir gecedir. O gece kadın erkek, genç yaşlı demeden meydanlara koşan milletimiz tankların, topların, mermilerin karşısında imanıyla, cesaretiyle ve vatan aşkıyla dimdik durmuştur. O gece ortaya konulan o eşsiz duruş yalnızca bir darbe girişiminin bertaraf edilmesi değil, aynı zamanda bu topraklarda esaretin asla kabul edilmeyeceğinin, milli iradenin üstünde hiçbir gücün bulunmayacağının en gür sesidir. Sizler her daim başımızın tacı, gözümüzün nurusunuz" dedi.
Gençlik ve Spor Bakan Yardımcısı Enes Eminoğlu, 253 şehidi rahmetle, minnetle andıklarını belirterek, bu milletin 1071 Malazgirt Savaşı'nda nasıl düşmana karşı çıktıysa, 15 Temmuz'da da ayrı iradeyle tanklara, uçaklara karşı çıktığını söyledi.
"Asırlık Gece" adlı yapım, Doç. Dr. Hüseyin Aydın’ın “Asırlık Gece” kitabından yola çıkılarak hazırlandı.
Vali Hulusi Şahin, şehit ailelerinin millet için taşıdığı değere vurgu yaparak, "Sizler bizim için çok değerlisiniz. Sizleri ailemizin bir ferdi olarak görüyoruz. Bu toplum, evlatlarını vatanı ve memleketi için gerektiğinde canını feda etmeye hazır olacak şekilde yetiştiriyor" dedi.
Şehit annelerinin vatan sevgisi ve fedakarlığının milletin gücünü ortaya koyduğunu ifade eden Vali Şahin, bir şehit annesinin, "Gerekirse, kaç çocuğum varsa o kadar çocuğumu vatan uğruna veririm" sözüne dikkat çekerek, "Bu millet yıkılmaz, bu millet yılmaz. Böyle analar olduğu müddetçe bu milletin başına hiçbir şey gelmez" diye konuştu.
Rüzgar Aksoy, "Asırlık Gece" filminde 15 Temmuz şehidi Astsubay Kıdemli Başçavuş Ömer Halisdemir’i canlandırdı.
“BU KADAR KAHRAMANA SAHİP BİR KİTLENİN İÇİNDE OLMAK GURUR VERİCİ”
“Asırlık Gece” filminde rol alan oyunculardan Rüzgar Aksoy, 10'uncu Şehit Aileleri Buluşması'na katıldığında şehit yakınları ve gazileri gördüğünde çok duygusal anlar yaşadığını belirtti.
15 Temmuz darbe girişiminin üzerinden 10 yıl geçtiğini belirten Rüzgar Aksoy, "Fakat hala insanların yüzleri gülse de gözlerinin derinliğinde kalp kırıklıklarını görüyorsunuz. Benim için gerçekten bu kadar kahramana sahip bir kitlenin içinde olmak gurur verici" dedi.
Konuşmaların ardından şehit yakınları ve protokol üyeleri “Asırlık Gece” filmini izledi.

Nazmi Sağlam ile çektiği videoyu sosyal medya hesabından paylaşan şarkıcı, "Geldim kızı buldum. Şimdi bisikleti almaya gidiyoruz" ifadelerini kullandı.
Videoda küçük kızın dedesine birden fazla bisiklet gönderileceğini söylediği için tepki gösteren Akalın, "Kaç tane bisiklet gelecek dedin niye öyle diyorsun ki? Bırak yollasınlar bisikletleri" dedi. Nazmi Sağlam ise "Gerek yok ki. Gerekmez bisiklet. Türkiye'mize teşekkür ediyoruz" sözleriyle karşılık verdi.

Bu sırada sürücünün annesi olduğu belirtilen kadın, bisikleti birkaç kez kaldırıp yere vurarak kırdı. Kızın annesiyle olay yerine gelmesi üzerine taraflar arasında tartışma yaşandı. O anlar bir iş yerinin güvenlik kamerasıyla kaydedildi.

Uzun süredir gözlerden uzak olan Okan Karacan'ın Şişli'de düzenlenen bir etkinlikte masanın üzerindeki dizüstü bilgisayarı aldığı öne sürüldü. Olaydan bir kaç gün sonra bilgisayarın sahibi olduğunu söyleyen E.Ş.A. bilgisayarı çalan kişinin Karacan olduğu iddiasıyla şikâyetçi oldu.
Olayla ilgili şüpheli olarak ifadesi alınan Okan Karacan ifadesinde, "Bilgisayarı yanlışlıkla aldım. 1 Mart tarihinde E.Ş.A. isimli kişi beraberinde 3 kişi ile birlikte gelerek beni darbetti. Beni kaçırıp aracın bagajına koydular, burada kafama silah kabzası ile 5 kez vurdular" iddiasında bulundu.
Ekipler, olayla ilgili Karacan'ın annesi İ.K.'nın da ifadesini aldı. Anne İ.K. ifadesinde, oğlunun olay günü iftar programına katıldıktan sonra eve bilgisayar ile geldiğini, bilgisayarın kendisine hediye edildiğini, birkaç gün sonra oğlu odasında uyurken, kapı çaldığını, Okan Karacan'ın kendisine bilgisayarı almaya geldiler, gelen kişiye bilgisayarı "ver" dediği öğrenildi.
Karacan'ın annesi ise bilgisayarı kapıya gelen kişiye verdiğini, oğlu Karacan'ın odasından hiç çıkmadığını ve gelen şahısla karşılaşmadığını, kimse tarafından zorla evden çıkartılmadığını ve darbedilmediğini, oğlunun psikolojik rahatsızlığı bulunduğunu, ilaç kullandığını, ancak bir süredir ilaçlarını düzenli kullanmayı bıraktığı için, dengesiz davranışlarının bulunduğunu öne sürdü.
Okan Karacan "açıktan hırsızlık" suçundan gözaltına alınarak 7 Mart günü adliyeye sevk edildi. Adliyeye sevk edilen Karacan serbest bırakıldı.
Olaydan aylar sonra güvenlik kamerası görüntüleri de ortaya çıktı. Görüntülerde Karacan'ın telefonla konuştuğu, masa üzerinde bulunan bilgisayarı inceledikten sonra koltuğunun altına alarak olay yerinden ayrıldığı görüntüler güvenlik kamerasına yansıdı.
Yaşananlardan aylar sonra Nişantaşı'nda görüntülenen Okan Karacan, hırsızlık iddiasıyla ilgili Behlül Aydın'a konuştu.
“Medyaya 30 senemi verdim. Halka mâl olmuş biri olarak bunu yapmak için deli olmak lazım” diyen Karacan, “Tamamen yanlış anlaşılma. Ekibimin cihazı olduğunu düşündüm. Evde anladık durumu. Ertesi gün teslim ettik” dedi.
Hakkındaki haberlere üzüldüğünü söyleyen Okan Karacan, "Bu görüntüyü kim yaydı, annemin söylemediğini kimler söylemiş gibi yazdı, inanılmaz üzüldüm. Ama olaydan sonra hem sanatçı hem de sevenlerimden destek gördüm. Bir şey cevap verince daha çok uzuyor. Yargısız infaz yapıldı” ifadelerini kullandı.

The BBC has lodged an "urgent" appeal against a US judge's decision to allow Donald Trump's $10bn (£7.6bn) lawsuit against the corporation to go ahead.
The US president is suing the BBC for defamation over the way an episode of Panorama edited a speech he gave in January 2021, shortly before the riot at the US Capitol.
Earlier this month, a federal judge in Florida ruled that the defamation case could proceed after the BBC sought to dismiss it.
The BBC has now filed an appeal with a higher court, saying there is a "complete lack of evidence" that anyone in Florida accessed the programme, and that the broadcaster made "rigorous and systematic efforts to prevent access to the documentary" in the US.
A BBC spokesman said: "We are surprised and disappointed by the court's decision that this case should be heard in Florida.
"As we have made clear from the start, the BBC broadcast this documentary in the UK - and UK only. We did not show it in Florida, nor did any other broadcaster.
"Given the urgency of this issue, we are now requesting a higher court review the ruling."
President Trump's lawsuit accuses the BBC of "intentionally, maliciously and deceptively doctoring" the speech he gave on 6 January 2021.
The BBC has apologised for the edit in Trump: A Second Chance, which it said had given "the mistaken impression that President Trump made a direct call for violent action".
But the corporation argued that the Panorama episode, which was broadcast in 2024, did not meet the legal criteria for defamation.
Earlier this month, federal judge Jeffrey T Kuntz found Trump's defamation allegations against the BBC sufficient for the case to continue, although he did not rule on the merits of the case.
President Trump called the judge's ruling a "huge victory" in a post on Truth Social at the time.
The BBC has now lodged an appeal with the US Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit, arguing that the Florida court has no jurisdiction to hear the case.
Trump has been ordered to answer questions under oath as part of the lawsuit by 22 January.
Judge Kuntz has scheduled a trial date for the case for 3 May 2027 in Fort Lauderdale, Florida.

Trabzon 'un Yomra ilçesinden geçen Şana Deresi'nin bir anda kırmızı akmaya başlaması, bölgede yaşayanları hem şaşırttı hem de tedirgin etti. Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği Bakanlığı, renk değişiminin kaynağını tespit ettiğini duyurdu. Bakanlığa göre dereyi kırmızıya çeviren, bölgedeki bir boya depolama tesisinin atıkları oldu. Tesisi işleten firmaya Çevre Kanunu kapsamında 2 milyon 346 bin lira idari para cezası kesildi.
Şana Deresi'nin rengindeki değişim kısa sürede yetkililere bildirildi. İhbarın ardından bölgeye Trabzon İl Tarım ve Orman Müdürlüğü ile jandarma ekipleri gönderildi. Suyun neden bu renge büründüğünü anlamak için dereden numuneler alındı ve laboratuvar incelemesi başlatıldı.
Aynı süreçte Trabzon Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği İl Müdürlüğü ekipleri de dere hattını adım adım taradı. Yapılan tespitlere göre bölgede faaliyet gösteren bir boya depolama tesisinin atıkları, mevzuata aykırı biçimde bertaraf edilmişti. Derenin kırmızıya dönmesinin sebebi de bu atıklar oldu.
İl Müdürlüğü ekipleri, tespitlerin ardından firmaya Çevre Kanunu'na dayanarak 2 milyon 346 bin liralık idari yaptırım uyguladı. Bakanlığın aktardığına göre son kontrollerde Şana Deresi'nin renginin yeniden düzeldiği görüldü.
Yomra'daki olay, Karadeniz'de birkaç gün arayla yaşanan ikinci benzer vaka oldu. 21 Kasım Cumartesi günü Rize 'deki Değirmendere Deresi'nin de rengi değişmişti. O olayda yapılan incelemede, renk değişiminin özel bir çay fabrikasından kontrolsüz şekilde boşaltılan atıklardan kaynaklandığı belirlenmişti.
Bakanlık, Rize'deki şirkete de idari para cezası uygulandığını açıklamış ancak cezanın tutarını duyurmamıştı. Bir hafta içinde iki farklı ilde yaşanan bu tablo, Karadeniz'deki derelerin üretim tesislerinden kaynaklanan atıklara karşı denetimini yeniden gündeme taşıdı.

Galatasaray'ın Rus yıldızı Aleksey Batrakov'un İstanbul'daki yaşamına dair ilginç bir detay ortaya çıktı. Genç futbolcunun memleketinde severek yediği geleneksel bir yemeği Türkiye'de özlemesi üzerine eşi Irina çözüm arayışına girdi. Ancak yemeği eşinin istediği kıvamda hazırlayamayan Irina, sonunda annesini İstanbul'a davet etti.
Rus mutfağının geleneksel lezzetlerinden patates zapekankaya düşkün olan Batrakov, Türkiye'ye geldikten sonra bu yemeği özlemeye başladı. Patates püresi, kıyma, soğan, tereyağı, yumurta ve sütle hazırlanan yemek, futbolcunun vazgeçilmezleri arasında yer alıyor.
Rus basınına konuşan eşi Irina, Batrakov'un isteği üzerine zapekanka yapmayı sık sık denediğini ancak bir türlü eşinin sevdiği kıvamı yakalayamadığını anlattı.
Eşinin denemeleri istediği sonucu vermeyince Irina, son çare olarak annesini İstanbul'a çağırdı. Kayınvalidesinin hazırladığı zapekankayı çok beğenen Rus futbolcu, özlediği ev yemeğine kavuştu.
Batrakov'un bu lezzete olan düşkünlüğü üzerine kayınvalidesi artık ayda bir İstanbul'a gelerek damadına patates zapekanka hazırlıyor.
Rus spor sitesi Sports.ru'da yer alan habere göre, Batrakov'un eşi İrina Podşibyakina, Smolov'un çektiği videoda futbolcunun en sevdiği yemeklerden birini yapmak için annesinden yardım istediğini anlattı.
İrina, Aleksey'in beslenmesi ve yemek yapıp yapmadığı sorulduğunda şöyle anlatıyor: “Yemek yapıyorum ama çok sık yaptığımı söyleyemem. Daha çok Aleksey için yemek hazırlıyorum. Canım isterse ona güzel bir sofra kurarım.
Anne babasının gelmesine o kadar sevindim ki anlatamam. Benden patates zapekanka yapmamı çok istiyordu. Bu yemeği daha önce bir kez güzel yapmıştım ama yemek konusunda kendimi çok eleştiriyorum. Tadı biraz hoşuma gitmese bile yeniden yapmaya çekiniyorum.
Ben ona en güzel yemekleri hazırlamak istiyorum.” Batrakov ise eşinin yemeklerini beğendiğini, zapekankayı tekrar tekrar istediğini söylüyor. İrina da annesi İstanbul'a geldiğinde ona, “Anne, lütfen, yalvarıyorum, bu işi çöz, ona zapekanka yap” dediğini anlatıyor. Sonunda yemek hazırlanıyor.

TV chef Gordon Ramsay is to lead the new presenting line-up on BBC motoring show Top Gear, which is being revived four years after it was last on air.
Ramsay will take the driving seat alongside as yet unnamed co-presenters when the show starts filming next year. It will return to screens in 2028.
The long-running programme has been off air since 2022, when co-host Andrew Flintoff suffered serious facial and rib injuries after his open-topped three-wheeled car overturned at the show's test-track.
In a statement announcing his new role, Ramsay said he wants to bring "a fresh energy and ambition" to the show's formula of being "surprising, entertaining and [with] just the right amount of chaos".
Andrew Flintoff, Paddy McGuinness and Chris Harris hosted the show before it was rested
Top Gear began in 1977 and became one of the BBC's biggest hits in the hands of Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May in the 2000s.
They were replaced by hosts including Chris Evans and Friends star Matt LeBlanc, before Flintoff took over in 2018 with Paddy McGuinness and Chris Harris.
But the show was "rested" after the former cricketer's crash in December 2022.
Flintoff was dragged face-down underneath the Morgan Super 3 car for about 50 metres. "I thought I was dead," he told a Disney+ documentary last year.
The BBC apologised and paid compensation to Flintoff following his crash.
In Wednesday's statement, Ramsay said he has had a love of cars since he grew up near the Silverstone race circuit in Northamptonshire.
"I would climb over the fences and sneak in for a glimpse of the racing," he said. "That early excitement sparked a lifelong passion for cars, motor sport, beautiful design and extraordinary engineering.
"At its very best Top Gear has always been about the unexpected - surprising, entertaining and just the right amount of chaos.
"That's the spirit we want to build on, bringing a fresh energy and ambition to create something truly thrilling for a whole new generation of audiences.
"It's an incredibly exciting opportunity, and I genuinely can't wait to get started!"
Former host Richard Hammond told BBC Radio 4's PM programme that Top Gear is "a grand old BBC stalwart".
"It goes back decades. We had our tenure of it and did our thing with it and went a bit crazy with it, and it'll be another incarnation of it," he said. "And great. It's a long runner, it'll carry on."
He said that he does not doubt Ramsay's credentials as a car fan, and joked that TV chefs "love three things: cooking - well in his case four - swearing, cooking, but also big watches and cars".
Hammond was seriously injured in a crash while filming the show in 2006, but said it "doesn't have to be" a dangerous show.
The BBC asked Hammond to return to the show for the new series, he said.
"They did talk to me about it. They came to me about maybe getting involved in leading the new Top Gear, and I don't want to drag it back to what it was. That's why I didn't do it," he said.
Ramsay drove in a celebrity race in Lego-themed cars at the Las Vegas Grand Prix at the weekend
Ramsay, 60, owns an extensive collection of cars including multiple Aston Martins and Ferraris, as well as a Porsche, Land Rover and McLaren Senna.
He has also appeared on Top Gear three times as a guest - in 2002, 2006 and 2017.
The BBC's director of entertainment Ed Havard said: "Gordon's fierce and fearless approach makes him a natural fit, and we're thrilled that audiences will see him in the driving seat as the show speeds into its next exciting era."
Suzy Lamb, managing director for BBC Studios Entertainment, added: "The return of Top Gear had to feel like a real TV event and Gordon fits the bill perfectly.
"He brings passion, mischief, genuine motoring credibility, and the kind of infectious competitive streak that defines the show at its best."
She promised that it "won't be a nostalgic reboot" but will be a "bold and unmissable new chapter for the most entertaining motoring show in the world".
Comedian Jimmy Carr was rumoured to have been in talks to join the hosting line-up, but was reported on Tuesday , external to have "pulled out".
Top Gear is the second high-profile show involving Ramsay to have been announced in the past week.
He has also been confirmed to star in a revival of Hell's Kitchen on ITV, hosted by Claudia Winkleman, more than two decades after he originally appeared on the celebrity cooking programme.
